`GET /api/accounts/{account_id}/members/manage-context` response (#139) — the

post.description: Leave an account you are a member of. Ends YOUR OWN membership only — the route takes no target, so it cannot be used on anyone else. AUTHORIZATION: no global permission is required, deliberately. Unlike the other member routes this does NOT require account::members::manage: revoking that capability turns self-service management off, and must not also trap existing members inside an account they want to leave. Authority is your own membership in THIS account, resolved per request — a non-member gets 404, identical to a nonexistent account id, and a personal account gets 422. Refuses (422 `LAST_OWNER`) if you are the account's sole owner: an account must keep at least one owner, so promote another member to `owner` first (see PATCH /accounts/{account_id}/members/{user_id}). Leaving also cancels every still-pending project transfer you are a party to on this account's projects, in the same transaction. Leaving does NOT delete or reassign the projects and datasets you created in the account — they stay with the account. FRONTEND NOTE (#149): do NOT gate a Leave affordance on `Account.membersManageContext` succeeding. That preflight requires account::members::manage AND the `admin` floor, so in the exact deployment where this route matters — self-service management switched off — it returns 403 while Leave is still available. Gate Leave on being a member, not on the management preflight; and note that a sole owner will get 422 `LAST_OWNER` here, which is a prompt to transfer ownership first, not an error to hide.

get.description: The account's membership audit ledger: who joined, left, was removed or was re-roled, when, and who did it. Paged, newest first. Requires account::members::manage AND account role `admin` or higher in THIS account — a non-member gets 404 (never 403), identical to a nonexistent account id; a bare `member` gets 403. THE LEDGER RECORDS COMPLETED MUTATIONS, NOT ATTEMPTS. Each row is written inside the same database transaction as the mutation it records, so a refused action (an escalation refused as ROLE_ABOVE_ACTOR, a removal refused as LAST_OWNER) leaves NO row at all. Read this as `what happened to this account`, never as `who tried what`. The rows are append-only and permanent — a correction is a new row, never an edit — and they are deleted only when the account itself is. This projection omits the unattended `system` provisioning event that seeds a new account, and on platform staff actions it reports `actor_kind: admin` WITHOUT the individual staff member's id: you learn that platform staff acted, not which employee. It does NOT omit every `system` event: a membership that ended with no attributable human actor — for example because the user account itself was deleted — is a real event in this account and IS shown, as `actor_kind: system`.

Requires account::members::manage AND account role `admin` or higher in THIS account; a non-member gets 404 (never 403), identical to a nonexistent account id. ROLE ESCALATION: the target's role must be at or below your own — 403 `ROLE_ABOVE_ACTOR` otherwise, so an admin cannot evict an owner. Refuses (422 `LAST_OWNER`) to remove the sole remaining owner. post.description: Invite an email address to an account you administer. Requires account::members::manage AND account role `admin` or higher in THIS account; a non-member gets 404 (never 403), identical to a nonexistent account id. ENUMERATION SAFETY — THIS IS A CONTRACT, NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL. This endpoint returns 202 with the body {"status":"sent"} and nothing else, IDENTICALLY, in all four cases: the address belongs to no user; it belongs to a user; it belongs to a user who is ALREADY A MEMBER of this account; a live invitation for it already exists (idempotent — the existing token stands). The last two are server-side no-ops. Do not add a distinguishing status or code for them: `409 ALREADY_A_MEMBER` would tell the caller both that the address is registered and that it is in this account, which is exactly the account-enumeration oracle invitations exist to avoid. THE INVITE LINK IS NOT IN THIS RESPONSE, deliberately — returning it only when a new invitation was created would itself be the oracle. The token is stored only as a SHA-256, so it cannot be re-derived later either: list the account's pending invitations with GET /accounts/{account_id}/invitations and mint a link with POST /accounts/{account_id}/invitations/{invitation_id}/resend. Put that token in the FRAGMENT of your invite URL (`/invite#<token>`), never in a path or query — a token in a URL leaks through Referer headers, browser history, proxy access logs and screen shares. ROLE CEILING: the role you request must be at or below your own role in this account — 403 `ROLE_ABOVE_ACTOR` otherwise, and no invitation is written. An admin may invite an `admin` or a `member`, but may not invite an `owner`. Accepting this invitation creates an account membership at the stated role. The role is FROZEN at issue — it is exactly what the invitee will receive, and it is never silently re-interpreted. Revoking the invitation before it is accepted withdraws the offer; it cannot withdraw a membership already created (remove the member instead). NOTE the redemption endpoint is NOT part of this release: until it ships, an invitation can be created, listed, resent and revoked, but not accepted. Account membership is an implicit grant: a `member` holds at least Viewer on EVERY project, dataset and artifact in the account, an `admin` holds Editor on all of them, and an `owner` holds Owner — including delete, transfer and share — on projects they did not create. Adding, removing or re-roling a member changes all of that in one call.

Distinguish by the error CODE. NOTE none of these depends on the email address you supplied

202.description:
`POST /api/accounts/{account_id}/invitations` response — **the same three bytes in
 every case**.

 `202 Accepted` with `{"status":"sent"}` whether the address belongs to no user, to a
 user, to a user who is already a member of this account, or already has a live
 invitation. The last two are server-side no-ops. The body is assembled from a single
 `const` in `handlers.rs`, so no branch can vary it.

 The `status` field exists only so the response is a JSON object rather than an empty
 body — a client that wants to branch on the outcome cannot, and that is the point.

That last rule is deliberate and is broader than it looks: the address is stored verbatim and will one day be placed in a mail header (so control characters must never reach the table), and an invisible character would make a second, distinct invitation for what a human reads as one address. It also means INTERNATIONALIZED addresses (SMTPUTF8 local parts, IDN domains) are refused; there is no mail transport in this product yet, and the right way to support them later is to normalize to the ASCII form at the boundary

post.description: Mint a FRESH token for a pending invitation and return it, pushing out the expiry. This is how you obtain an invite link: the token is stored only as a SHA-256, so the server cannot reproduce a link it has already handed out, and the create response deliberately carries none. Resending INVALIDATES the previous token — any link already circulated stops working. Put the returned token in the FRAGMENT of your invite URL (`/invite#<token>`), never in a path or query string: fragments are never sent to a server, so the token stays out of Referer headers, proxy access logs and browser history. Requires account::members::manage AND account role `admin` or higher in THIS account. Keyed on the invitation id within THIS account, so an invitation belonging to another account, an unknown id, and an already-accepted, revoked or expired invitation are all the same 404. ROLE CEILING: the invitation's frozen role must be at or below your own — 403 `ROLE_ABOVE_ACTOR` otherwise, so an admin cannot refresh an `owner` invitation issued by someone who outranked them. (Revoking one is deliberately NOT gated that way: revoking removes no role.)

`POST /api/accounts/{account_id}/invitations/{invitation_id}/resend` response.

 **This is the only place a plaintext invitation token is ever surfaced**, and it is
 surfaced to the inviter, who is an `admin` or `owner` of the account the invitation
 belongs to. It is enumeration-safe because the operation is keyed by invitation ID —
 an id the caller obtained by listing their own account's invitations — and takes no
 email, so there is nothing to probe.

429.description: `INVITATION_RATE_LIMITED` — a resend MINTS a token, so it records one mint exactly as a create does and is counted by the same per-actor and per-account windows, one for one, with no exemption for the first resend. NOTE the ceilings are expressed in MINTS: because the create response carries no link, one usable invitation costs one create plus one resend, so the reachable rate of usable invitations is about half the stated ceiling

delete.description: Revoke a pending invitation. SOFT: the row is stamped `revoked_at`/ `revoked_by` and kept, never deleted, so the audit trail survives. Afterwards the token stops resolving and the address may be invited afresh. Requires account::members::manage AND account role `admin` or higher in THIS account. Keyed on the invitation id within THIS account, so a foreign, unknown or already-settled id is the same 404 — a second revoke included. There is deliberately NO role ceiling on revoke, unlike create and resend: revoking removes no role (the invitee holds nothing yet), so there is no standing to be above, and gating it would stop a lower-ranked admin cleaning up an `owner` invitation someone else left behind. Revoking withdraws the OFFER. It cannot withdraw a membership already created by an acceptance — remove the member instead (DELETE /accounts/{account_id}/members/{user_id}).

404.description: You are not a member of this account, or it does not exist; or the invitation does not exist, belongs to another account, or is already SETTLED (accepted, or already revoked). All INDISTINGUISHABLE. NOTE an EXPIRED but unsettled invitation is NOT in this set — it revokes with a 204, which makes revoke the one route on which "an expired invitation with this id exists here" differs from "no such id". That is not an oracle (reaching either requires being an admin of the account, who can already list its invitations) but it is a difference, and it is a decision rather than a surprise

post.description: Redeem an invitation token and join the account it names. AUTHENTICATED, but NOT account-scoped and NOT permission-gated: the redeemer is by definition not yet a member of the account, so the TOKEN is the capability. THE TOKEN GOES IN THE BODY. This operation declares no path, query or header parameter, deliberately — a token in a URL leaks through Referer headers, browser history, proxy access logs and screen shares. The invite link a client builds must carry the token in the URL FRAGMENT (`/invite#<token>`), which is never sent to a server; the SPA reads the fragment and POSTs it here. SIGNUP-THEN-ACCEPT: an invitee with no account should hold the token in memory (not in localStorage, not in the URL), register through POST /api/auth/register — which is UNCHANGED by this change and must never be given token handling — and then call this endpoint. If they register with a DIFFERENT address than the one invited, this endpoint returns the generic 404 below; that is correct, and the UI should say which address the invitation was sent to, which is safe to show to a holder of a valid token. INDISTINGUISHABLE FAILURES — THIS IS A CONTRACT, NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL: a wrong token, an expired token, an already-redeemed token, a revoked token, and a valid token presented by a user whose email does not match all return the SAME 404 with a BYTE-IDENTICAL body. Never add a distinguishing code or message for any of them — the difference is exactly what a token grinder wants, and `expired` alone confirms that a valid token once existed for that account. EMAIL BINDING: the authenticated user's email, normalized, must equal the invitation's. Emails are not verified in this deployment, so this is containment against a leaked link reaching the wrong logged-in tab, NOT proof of identity. Account membership is an implicit grant: a `member` holds at least Viewer on EVERY project, dataset and artifact in the account, an `admin` holds Editor on all of them, and an `owner` holds Owner — including delete, transfer and share — on projects they did not create. Adding, removing or re-roling a member changes all of that in one call.

 **The token travels in the BODY, and nowhere else** (INV-18, research §4.2): a token in
 a URL path or query leaks through `Referer` headers, browser history, proxy access logs
 and screen shares. The link the invitee opens is a FRONTEND route carrying the token in
 the URL **fragment** (`/invite#<token>`) — fragments are never sent to a server — and the
 SPA reads it and POSTs it here.

 The route declares no path or query parameter at all, so this struct is the only place
 the token can arrive; a test asserts that against the SHIPPED `openapi.json` rather than
 against this comment.

201.description: Joined. Exactly one account_members row was created, the invitation was stamped accepted, and an audit row was written — all in one transaction.

200.description: You were ALREADY a member of that account. Idempotent: no second membership row, and your role is unchanged — an invitation never promotes an existing member. The invitation is consumed, so the token is now spent. `role` is your actual role, which may differ from the one the invitation named.

403.description: ROLE_ABOVE_ACTOR — the person who sent this invitation no longer has the standing to confer it: they have been removed from the account, demoted below `admin`, or demoted below the role the invitation confers. The role ceiling is re-checked AT REDEMPTION, not only at issue, so an `owner` invitation from an owner who has since been demoted does not land days later. No membership is created and the invitation is left pending. Distinguishable from the 404 on purpose: you have already proved you hold a valid token addressed to you, so there is nothing left to enumerate.

404.description: INVALID_INVITATION — the one generic refusal. Returned identically, with a byte-identical body, for: no such token; an expired token; an already-redeemed token; a revoked token; and a valid token whose invited address does not match your account's email.

422.description: SEAT_LIMIT_REACHED — the account is at its plan's member allowance; `details` carries plan_id, limit and current so the UI can offer the upgrade path. Nothing is written and the invitation stays PENDING, so it can be redeemed once a seat frees. Or PERSONAL_ACCOUNT_NOT_MANAGEABLE — a personal account has exactly one member, its owner, and no membership surface.

bearerAuth.description: JWT obtained from POST /auth/login or POST /auth/register, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

AcceptInvitationRequest.description:
`POST /api/account-invitations/accept` request (#146).

 **The token travels in the BODY, and nowhere else** (INV-18, research §4.2): a token in
 a URL path or query leaks through `Referer` headers, browser history, proxy access logs
 and screen shares. The link the invitee opens is a FRONTEND route carrying the token in
 the URL **fragment** (`/invite#<token>`) — fragments are never sent to a server — and the
 SPA reads it and POSTs it here.

 The route declares no path or query parameter at all, so this struct is the only place
 the token can arrive; a test asserts that against the SHIPPED `openapi.json` rather than
 against this comment.

token.description:
The base64url invitation token, exactly as it appeared in the invite link's
 fragment. Only its SHA-256 is ever compared against storage; the plaintext is never
 written anywhere.

AcceptInvitationResponse.description:
`POST /api/account-invitations/accept` response (#146).

 Deliberately minimal — the account id and the caller's role in it, which is what a
 client needs to switch into the account it just joined. Everything else arrives the way
 the rest of this module delivers state: a `SyncEntity::AccountMember` frame followed by
 the client's own `GET /api/accounts` (`account/sync.rs` — notify-and-refetch, no row
 data on the wire).

 `role` is the membership's ACTUAL role. On the idempotent already-a-member path (`200`
 rather than `201`) that is the role the caller already held, not the invitation's — an
 invitation never promotes an existing member (#146 DEC-12).

Account.description:
An `accounts` row. `personal_user_id` is the owning user for a `personal`
 account, `None` for an `organization` (enforced by the DB CHECK
 `accounts_personal_has_user`).

AccountKind.description:
What KIND of account this is (the personal/org discriminator, DEC-1). A text
 `kind` (not a boolean) so a third kind can be added without a schema change and
 so metering/billing read a stable, self-documenting discriminator.

oneOf.description:
The single, never-disabled account auto-created per user (owns their
 resources by default). Exactly one per user (INV-1).
A shared account many users join (the SaaS org). Created by A3 (`saas`).

AccountListResponse.description:
`GET /api/accounts` response — the caller's account memberships (the switcher
 list). Owner-filtered by `list_user_accounts` (never a cross-account leak).

AccountMember.description:
An `account_members` row — one `(account, user)` membership edge with its
 coarse role. `PRIMARY KEY (account_id, user_id)` is the one-membership-per-pair
 constraint.

display_name.description:
The member's chosen display name (`users.display_name`, NULLABLE) — the
 preferred primary label when present. `None` ⇒ the UI falls back to `username`.

email.description: The member's email (`users.email`, NOT NULL) — the secondary identity line.

username.description:
The member's login handle (`users.username`, NOT NULL) — the UI's fallback
 primary label when `display_name` is absent. Enriches the response so a human
 reads a person, never the bare `user_id` UUID (#51 defect #1).

AccountMemberEvent.description:
One row of the membership audit ledger (#148), as served by the two read routes.

 **This is a projection, not the stored row.** The account-scoped route
 (`GET /api/accounts/{account_id}/members/events`) applies three subtractions IN SQL, while
 the staff route (`GET /api/admin/accounts/{account_id}/members/events`) serves the full row:

 1. the unattended `system` event that SEEDS a new account is omitted — but NOT every
    `system` event: a membership that ended with no attributable human actor (for example
    because the user account itself was deleted) is a real event in this account and IS
    shown, as `actor_kind: system`;
 2. on platform-staff actions `actor_user_id` is NULL — you learn that staff acted, not
    which employee;
 3. `reason` is never selected.

 Applying them in SQL rather than in a serializer is why a later caller cannot reach a
 redacted column by constructing this struct differently.

 **This doc-comment is the SHIPPED schema description.** `JsonSchema` emits it verbatim into
 `openapi.json` and the generated `types.ts`, so a stale sentence here reaches every client —
 which is exactly how the first version of subtraction (1) went out contradicting the
 operation description in the same document, with the contract test green because it read
 only the operation half.

 **What it records, and what it does not.** A row exists for a membership mutation that
 COMMITTED. A refused attempt leaves nothing — the write shares the mutation's transaction,
 so a refusal rolls it back. Read this as "what happened to this account", never as "who
 tried what".

actor_kind.description:
`user` (a principal acting with no more authority than their own membership) |
 `admin` (a principal acting with the platform-staff capability, wherever that
 capability is checked — not merely a URL prefix) | `system` (no human actor is
 attributable: the provisioning hook, or a membership ended by the `users` FK cascade).
 Never absent — a staff action must be distinguishable from an owner's, and an
 unattributable one from both.

actor_user_id.description:
Who acted. NULL for a system action, and — on the ACCOUNT-scoped route only — NULL for
 a staff action too: an account admin learns that platform staff acted, not which
 employee. The staff identity is stored and is served on the admin surface.

invitation_id.description: Ties an `invited` event to the `joined` that answered it.

old_role.description:
Both present on `role_changed`; `old_role` alone on a removal; `new_role` alone on a
 join.

reason.description: Staff-authored note. Always absent on the account-scoped route (#148 DEC-7).

target_email.description:
The invitation address, for an invitee who has no account yet. Trimmed and otherwise
 stored verbatim (it is NOT lowercased — the local part is case-sensitive and this row is
 permanent). Mutually exclusive with `target_user_id` by CHECK constraint.

target_user_id.description:
Whom it happened to. NULL only for an invitation sent to an ADDRESS that has no user
 yet — an invitation to somebody already in the directory names them by id instead, and
 then carries no address. Exactly one of `target_user_id` and `target_email` is set, for
 every action.

AccountMemberEventsResponse.description:
The membership-audit read response — paged with the same numbered settings-list idiom as
 [`AccountMembersResponse`], so a client pages both surfaces identically.

AccountMembersManageContext.description:
`GET /api/accounts/{account_id}/members/manage-context` response (#139) — the
 caller's member-management standing in ONE account.

 Reaching this response at all IS the authorization proof: it is served behind
 `AccountScope<RoleAdmin>`, so the caller has been shown to hold
 `account::members::manage` AND to rank `admin` or above in THIS account. It is the
 preflight a management UI runs before rendering write affordances — the global
 `usePermission(Permissions.AccountMembersManage)` answers only half the question.

account_id.description:
The account this answer is about — echoes the PATH id, never the
 `X-Account-Id` header (which is ignored on this surface; DEC-1).

actor_role.description: The caller's REAL role in this account (`admin` or `owner` here, by the floor).

member_count.description: How many members the account currently has.

AccountMembersResponse.description:
`GET /api/accounts/{id}/members` response — one org's members, paged (the
 settings-list numbered-pagination idiom; `total` drives "Showing N of M").

AccountRole.description:
The acting user's COARSE role on an account (DEC / INV-4). `Ord` is
 `Owner > Admin > Member` (derived from declaration order below), so
 [`AccountRole::allows`] grades a minimum-role floor. Distinct from the
 within-resource ACL `EffectivePermission` (viewer/editor).

AckResponse.description:
Uniform ack for the agent up-endpoints. `ok: false` means the request did
 not correlate to something owned by the caller — a `request_id` with no
 pending dispatch (already resolved / timed out / never existed / owned by
 another user), or a `connection_id` that is no longer the caller's bound
 control connection. Not an error the engine needs to retry, just
 informational.

AgentCapabilitiesBody.description:
`POST /api/mcp/agent/capabilities` body — the controlled session REPLACES
 its VIEW-SCOPED capability set (`modules/mcp/capabilities.rs`).

capabilities.description:
The FULL current set, not a delta: an add-only protocol could never
 express a removal, and the browser holds the authoritative registry.

connection_id.description:
The server-minted connection id the SSE `connected` handshake handed
 THIS session. The report is accepted only while this still identifies
 the user's bound control connection — a superseded tab (a reload racing
 a rebind) must not overwrite the live session's catalog. Deliberately
 NOT the client-supplied `session_id`, which a reload legitimately
 persists (see `agent_channel::ControlSession::conn_id`).

data.description:
Optional structured payload alongside `message`. Accepted for
 CONTRACT.md parity; not yet surfaced anywhere (no streamed-progress
 channel back to the LLM this slice — see `handlers.rs`'s module doc).

AnalysisParameters.description:
The analysis parameters: the decision day and the baseline window end
 (2026-10-19 contract: a draw is baseline when day ≤ `baseline_max_day`;
 pre-treatment negative days count as baseline). Per-analysis user inputs
 (screen B/C), never operational tunables (DEC-9); defaults apply when the
 UI omits the block.

AuthProviderResponse.description:
Admin-view summary of an auth provider. The `config` JSONB is
 returned with `client_secret` and any sensitive key contents
 MASKED — see handlers.rs::mask_provider_config.

last_test_at.description: When the admin last clicked Test on this row (null = never).

last_test_message.description: Human-readable detail from the last test.

last_test_ok.description: Outcome of the last test (null = never tested).

BlobType.description: Helper type for documenting binary responses in OpenAPI

CatalogueEnv.description:
The benchmark container-image reference the catalogue carries as DATA (the
 runtime `EnvRef` is built from `method-env-images.json` — a different
 artifact; see the PLAN's env note). The image string carries no scheme and is
 never fetched by this module.

ChangePasswordRequest.description:
Self-service password change for the authenticated user. Requires
 the current password as proof. Only valid for local-password
 accounts (`password_hash IS NOT NULL`).

CovariateColumn.description:
One covariate column's numeric-ness fact (an inspect-time report: a
 covariate known to a numeric rule is a usable covariate; a text column is
 a covariate the engine cannot use as a number).

CovariateFacts.description:
The covariate facts of a saved model: the catalogue's mode + whether the
 run actually ran with covariates on (both recorded at save — the J screen's
 "uses age" is `used`, never a re-derivation).

CovariateMode.description: Whether a method's inputs include patient covariates beyond the markers.

Coverage.description:
Per-patient coverage aggregate (no per-patient payload in the response —
 coverage facts only).

CreateAuthProviderResponse.description:
Response body for `POST /admin/auth-providers`. Wraps the persisted
 row in an envelope so we can attach a `connection_warning` when a
 create-time probe failed and the row was auto-downgraded to
 `enabled=false`. Mirrors `llm_repository`'s create-response shape.

connection_warning.description:
Populated when the provider was created with `enabled=true` but
 the connection probe failed; the row is persisted with
 `enabled=false` and this carries the failure reason so the UI
 can render an inline warning. `null` on the happy path.

email.description:
The address to invite. Normalized (`lower(trim(…))`) before anything is done with
 it; an empty/whitespace-only value is a 400.

role.description:
The account role the invitation will confer. Must be at or below the caller's own
 role in this account — 403 `ROLE_ABOVE_ACTOR` otherwise (R-1, #142).

CreateInvitationResponse.description:
`POST /api/accounts/{account_id}/invitations` response — **the same three bytes in
 every case**.

 `202 Accepted` with `{"status":"sent"}` whether the address belongs to no user, to a
 user, to a user who is already a member of this account, or already has a live
 invitation. The last two are server-side no-ops. The body is assembled from a single
 `const` in `handlers.rs`, so no branch can vary it.

 The `status` field exists only so the response is a JSON object rather than an empty
 body — a client that wants to branch on the outcome cannot, and that is the point.

CreateOrganizationRequest.description:
`POST /api/accounts` request — create an ORGANIZATION account (#34). `owner_id`
 defaults to the caller (the creator becomes the owner); an admin may name a
 different existing user as the owner. Gated `account::manage`.

name.description: The organization's display name (trimmed; must be non-empty).

owner_id.description: The user to seed as the `owner` member. Defaults to the caller when absent.

CreateRunRequest.description:
`POST /api/txr/runs` — the run the engine persists and drives. One
 analysis = one run row holding the analysis config + the input snapshot +
 the selected methods (train) or the resolved model assets (reuse).

method_ids.description: Train mode: the selected catalogue method ids (≥ 1 — validate()).

model_ids.description:
Reuse mode: the resolved model assets (`model-store`'s join shape,
 DEC-10 — assets are DATA to the engine, never an import).

DeleteEnvQuery.description:
The `?prune=true` flag of `DELETE /api/sandbox/envs/{env_id}` — separate
 from the delete itself so "forget the download state" and "also reclaim the
 cached artifact" are two explicit intents (DEC-17: prune on demand only).

DownloadCancelQuery.description:
The cancel/prune query (`?prune=true` removes the cached file for the
 entry's digest — DEC-17's explicit prune).

prune.description: Also remove the cached file for the entry's digest.

DownloadTokenGenQuery.description:
Query for minting a download token. Optionally pin a specific version so the
 resulting token downloads that exact version's bytes (the version number is
 baked into the SIGNED claims — a head token can't be repurposed to fetch
 other versions).

EligibilityRequest.description:
The eligibility request body — a tagged union carrying exactly one of the two
 request kinds (`{"preview": …}` or `{"inventory": …}`).

EligibilityResponse.description: The eligibility response — per-method verdicts plus the screen-B totals.

total_no_env.description:
The `cannot_run` methods whose reason is
 [`ReasonCode::EnvImageMissing`] — the count of catalogue methods the
 app cannot actually start (no published environment available), so the
 list header can say how many exist while still
 listing them.

EligibilityStatus.description:
The three-method eligibility verdict vocabulary (the board's "Can run / Can
 run for some patients / Cannot run").

EnvIndexStatus.description:
`GET /api/sandbox/envs` (PROV-SS-5): the stack half + the two env indexes.

 The `base`/`layers` split is THIS route's classification job — an
 [`EnvKind::Unknown`] record belongs to neither list (DRIFT-1 #15: the
 manager never guesses base/layer, so an unknown entry only answers the
 per-env `status` route).

oneOf.description:
A trimmed per-language base rootfs
 (`ghcr.io/tinnlab/txresbench-env/…`).
A per-method layer image (`ghcr.io/tinnlab/txr-method-env-layers/…`).

The env has never been ensured in this process and is not persisted, so
 the manager cannot know whether it is a base or a layer. This node is
 deliberately catalogue-free (it never enumerates env names); the caller
 of [`MethodEnvManager::status`] knows the kind from its own records.
 A `Unknown` record is never mounted — `ensure` refuses it.

EnvRef.description:
Reference to one sandboxed artifact (base rootfs or method layer).

 `digest` is the 64-hex sha256 of the artifact's single squashfs layer, taken
 from the caller's catalogue record — verification is always against THIS
 value, never against a moving tag (DEC-3).

digest.description:
The pinned 64-hex sha256 of the squashfs layer the bytes are verified
 against.

oci_ref.description:
Full OCI reference, e.g. `<prefix>/<env_id>[:<tag>][@sha256:<hex>]`
 (prefixes from [`TXR_BASE_REGISTRY_PREFIX`] /
 [`TXR_LAYER_REGISTRY_PREFIX`]; enforced by [`validate_oci_ref`]).

tag.description: Optional tag; resolved only when the reference carries no `@digest`.

EstimateRequest.description:
The estimate request: which methods, on how many patients, on how many
 CPUs, running `at_a_time` lanes.

cpus.description:
The CPU count an estimate is scaled to. Absent (or `null`) means the
 run's own resolution — the host's detected CPUs ([`estimate::host_cpus`],
 the ONE implementation the execution engine's run-start detection also
 calls), so the bar and the running header always employ the same count.
 A present value is used as posted (0 is rejected).

EstimateResponse.description:
The estimate response: per-method seconds, the plain sum, and the
 longest-processing-time schedule total over the `at_a_time` lanes (the
 bottom-bar "about X minutes in total"). `cpus` is the
 count actually used (the posted value, or the run's own resolution —
 [`estimate::host_cpus`] — when omitted), so the consumer can show the
 number the estimate was scaled to.

ExampleSetResponse.description:
The example saved set's answer (qa-fixes3 ITEM-3): the caller asks "give me
 the example models" and gets the set id when it exists, the creating run's
 id + status while it trains (the call reports the run's job state — the
 UI polls it),
 or the failed reason. `methods` is the deterministic fast-method pick the
 set was (or is being) trained with.

methods.description:
The deterministic fast-method pick (the plan's "3 that run in under
 30 s each").

ExampleSetState.description:
The example saved set's state (qa-fixes3 ITEM-3, `POST
 /api/txr/models/example`): `creating` (the run is training the methods),
 `ready` (the set exists) or `failed` (the honest reason is in the
 response's `error`; the next call retries).

ExportTarget.description:
The one-off export record of a save (PROV-MS-3's `also_export` arm) — the
 file is already written; `dir` is where the user's "Open the folder" points.

FeatureFlagView.description:
One flag as presented on the admin surface: the compiled registry facts plus the
 current global/per-account rows and the RESOLVED effective value for the queried
 account (or the global effective value when no account was queried).

account_enabled.description:
The per-account override's value for the queried account, if one exists (and
 only when an `account_id` was queried). `null` otherwise.

default_enabled.description: The compiled default (the value when no DB row overrides it).

effective.description:
The resolved value: per-account override → global → compiled default. When an
 `account_id` was queried this is that account's effective value; otherwise it
 is the global effective value.

global_enabled.description:
The GLOBAL row's value, if a global row exists (else `null` → the compiled
 default applies globally).

FeaturesListQuery.description:
Optional `?account_id=` for the flag list — resolve the effective/per-account
 columns for this account instead of the global view.

account_id.description:
The account the `effective`/`account_enabled` columns were resolved for
 (`?account_id=`), or `null` for the global view.

File.description:
File entity — the **head view** of a versioned file. The per-version columns
 (`file_size`, `mime_type`, …) reflect the current head version: `files`
 keeps them as a denormalized mirror that `append_version`/`restore_version`
 update in lock-step, so every existing reader of `files.*` transparently
 sees the latest version.

blob_version_id.description:
Storage key for the head version's bytes — equals `current_version_id`
 for a normal head, or the restored target for a restored head. Internal
 resolution detail (callers load blobs by this id).

FileColumns.description: The column-resolution report of one file (PROV-FV-2's `columns`).

covariate_columns.description:
The covariate columns with their numeric-ness (the model's covariate
 input fact: a non-numeric covariate column is not usable as one).

resolved.description:
role wire-key (`patient_id`, `pfs_days`, … `covariate:<name>`) →
 column name, for every column that matched a rule alias (DEC-5).

unresolved.description: Columns known to no rule — reported, never rejected (DEC-5).

FileInspection.description:
The inspect response (PROV-FV-2). The problems cover the per-file checks
 (types, nullability, uniqueness, cross-table references that are
 resolvable single-file, header and required-column problems); the full
 cross-table + join + units + outcome set is the `validate` response's.

FileInspectionRequest.description:
The inspect request body: ONE file, no cross-file context (screen C inspects
 each file as it is dropped; screen N inspects its only file — INV-3).

FileOutcomes.description:
The file's outcome-column facts — the availability of the four outcome
 column kinds the validator resolves (`responder`/`response_day` for the
 response task, `pfs_*`/`os_*` event + time for the survival task). The
 engine needs them to emit the three outcome-availability verdicts
 (`RESPONSE_LABEL_MISSING`, `SURVIVAL_OUTCOME_MISSING`,
 `TASK_INCOMPATIBLE` — PROV-MC-5's grown vocabulary); they are facts the
 validator knows and puts on the inventory it posts.

has_event.description: The file carries a survival event column (`pfs_event`/`os_event`).

has_responder.description: The file carries a `responder` column (per patient).

has_response_day.description: The file carries a `response_day` column (per patient).

has_survival_day.description: The file carries a survival time column (`pfs_days`/`os_days`).

FileProblem.description:
One reported problem (INV-2: every problem carries its FILE row — 1-based,
 header included — or `null` for file-level; columns are named when the
 problem is a column's, `null` otherwise).

FileSummary.description:
The file-level summary facts of an inspect call (row count, marker columns
 and their row counts, the distinct draw days).

FileTableKind.description:
The two user-file tables (screen C and screen N) — one parsed shape, both
 screens, one validation pipeline (INV-3).

FileVersion.description: One immutable version of a file.

blob_version_id.description: Storage key for this version's bytes (= `id`, or the restored target).

source_message_id.description: The chat turn / tool-call that produced this version (provenance).

FrontendActionEntry.description:
One frontend action. Field names match CONTRACT.md's `frontend-actions.json`
 schema exactly — the SAME shape whether the entry came from the committed
 app-owned manifest or was REPORTED by the controlled browser session
 (`modules/mcp/capabilities.rs`), so `handlers.rs` has ONE code path.

 This is ALSO the wire shape a session reports (`AgentCapabilitiesBody`). One
 shape, one type: a parallel wire struct would be a second definition of the
 same thing, which is the defect class this module's history is made of. What
 the wire direction adds is not a type but a GATE — the report is untrusted
 input, filtered and bounded by `capabilities::sanitize` before it can reach
 the catalog.

context.description:
Which app CONTEXT (active page/surface) must be live for this action to
 be invokable — `"global"` (always available) or a named context such as
 `"workbench"`/`"dataset"` (workbench-analysis PLAN.md ITEM-4). Surfaced
 by `describe_capability` as a precondition so the AI navigates there
 first; the ENGINE enforces the `CONTEXT_INACTIVE` reject and the backend
 merely RELAYS it (this catalog only carries the value through — the exact
 Layer 5/6 split the `stateful` field follows for staleness).
 `#[serde(default = "default_context")]` keeps a manifest predating this
 field parseable, defaulting to `"global"` — the same back-compat the
 `stateful` field's `#[serde(default)]` provides.

group.description:
Discoverability metadata (richer-actions ITEM-4) — the display GROUP, a
 one-line DESCRIPTION, and ALTERNATIVE search terms (aliases/keywords) the
 frontend `defineAction` carries. Surfaced to the agent by
 `list_capabilities` (searched) + `describe_capability` (shown) so it can
 find/pick an action by intent, not only its exact title. Each
 `#[serde(default)]` keeps a manifest predating these fields parseable
 (the `stateful`/`context` back-compat precedent).

kind.description:
`"global"` (invoked directly by id) or `"instance"` (addresses a
 runtime `view_id` — ai-actions slice 3, ARCHITECTURE.md Layer 4).
 Branched on in `handlers.rs`'s `invoke_frontend`/`describe_capability`
 to thread `view_id`/`expected_token` through to the agent channel.

stateful.description:
Only meaningful when `kind == "instance"`. `true` together with
 `mutating` means invoking this action requires a valid `expected`
 state token (the read-before-write / stale-state guard,
 ARCHITECTURE.md Layer 6) — engine-enforced, this catalog only carries
 the flag through to `describe_capability` + the invoke path.
 `#[serde(default)]` keeps a manifest predating this field parseable.

ImportOutcome.description:
`POST /api/txr/models/import` (201) — the restored rows + the set they were
 imported into. `set_id` is null when the multipart carried no `set_id`
 form field (the container's recorded set is then recreated fresh); the
 reader's default-set rule lives in `store.rs`.

InventoryCovariate.description: One covariate column of the file inventory.

key.description: The file column key (the validator's stable key).

InventoryEligibilityRequest.description:
The file-inventory body (screens C/N/E — the consumer that holds the file
 posts it).

outcomes.description:
The outcome-column facts of the file, when the consumer knows them
 (absence skips the outcome-availability checks — a request without them
 is not misclassified by the engine).

InventoryMarker.description: One marker column of the file inventory.

has_detection_companion.description:
The column has a `__detected`/`__lod` companion (data.py's companion
 semantics — companions never rank or match).

is_detection_call.description: The column is a detection call (present/absent, not a measured value).

key.description: The file column key (the validator's stable key).

per_patient.description:
Per-patient draw counts; OMITTED when the validator does not carry them
 (coverage then falls back to the patient-level counts above).

InvitationSummary.description:
One row of `GET /api/accounts/{account_id}/invitations` — the inviter's view of their
 OWN account's pending invitations.

 **What is deliberately ABSENT is the specification, not an oversight.** There is no
 `user_id`, no `username`, no `display_name`, no `registered` flag and no token or
 hash. Issue #145: *"The list response must never reveal whether a pending invitee is a
 registered user — return the email as typed, `role`, `created_at`, `expires_at`,
 `invited_by`, and nothing user-shaped."* The SQL behind it never joins `users`, so the
 property holds by construction rather than by a projection someone must remember to
 keep narrow.

 **There is no invite LINK here either**, and that follows from the token being hashed
 at rest: the server cannot reproduce a link it has already handed out. The link is
 minted afresh by `POST …/invitations/{id}/resend` (#145 DEC-2).

email.description: The normalized address the invitation was issued to.

invited_by.description:
The inviter's user id — an audit field, not a live reference (the column has no
 FK, so this may name a user who has since been deleted).

InvitationsListResponse.description:
`GET /api/accounts/{account_id}/invitations` response — paged (the settings-list
 numbered-pagination idiom; `total` drives "Showing N of M").

JoinOffer.description:
A join offer the user accepted: every `variants` spelling of one logical
 marker column merges into the single `key` (DEC-12: nothing is ever
 auto-applied — an `A03` problem is a QUESTION; the user's `joins[]` entry
 is the answer).

password.description:
User's existing local password — the auth proof for binding
 the social identity.

ListVersionsQuery.description:
Optional pagination for the versions list. Defaults bound an
 un-paginated caller to the most recent `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE` versions
 (newest first) instead of returning an unbounded set.

LocalSession.description:
The minted session for the single local owner, shape-compatible with the
 desktop `auto_login` command's return.

provider.description:
Optional provider name for LDAP/OAuth authentication
 If not specified, defaults to local password authentication

MarkerColumn.description:
One resolved marker column of the file (after joins and mappings) — the
 per-marker facts the C/N card renders and the inventory is built from.

key.description: The stable column key (the join key after merges).

spellings.description:
Every spelling that merged into this key (`["ldh", "LDH"]` after a
 join — EXAMPLE-FV-1).

vocabulary.description: The vocabulary candidates (join offers) — suggestions, never applied.

MarkerCoverage.description:
The per-marker coverage counts (EXAMPLE-FV-3: the board's "needs 3 or more
 draws; 120 of 151 have them" is renderable from these three numbers).

MarkerFacts.description:
The marker-input facts recorded on a saved model at save time (the
 catalogue's [`MarkerKind`]/[`UsesHistory`] vocabulary verbatim — a model
 INSTANCE's facts, since the D5-selected feature set is per instance).

MarkerGroup.description: One of the 7 board marker groups (screen B checkbox row).

MarkerKind.description:
The marker-input shape of a method: `any` (marker-agnostic; `count` 0 =
 unbounded), `single` (1 marker), `panel` (N named markers from a fixed list),
 `multi` (N markers, no fixed list).

MarkerMapping.description:
A vocabulary mapping the user confirmed: file column `key` is the
 vocabulary marker `marker_id` (DEC-12: mapping is explicit only; fuzzy
 suggestions are never applied without it).

MarkerMatch.description:
One vocabulary candidate for a file marker column (the join offer's
 "this column looks like X" fact — PROV-FV-3's `MarkerMatch`).

marker_id.description: The vocabulary marker's id within its system.

n_methods.description:
How many runnable methods reference this marker (the join-offer
 weight — a marker 300 methods rank differently from one 3 do).

system.description:
The raw registry system spelling (`LOINC`, `HGNC`, … — the open-string
 system, same as `StandardId.system`, never a closed list here).

MarkerSummary.description: One marker column's inspect summary (name → value-row count).

MarkerSystem.description:
The marker identifier system of a vocabulary marker (the registry's systems;
 the matching engine also knows the `other`-system fallback as an open string).

MarkerVocabularyResponse.description:
The marker-vocabulary response (the join-offer + the B-screen group-panel
 vocabulary; the checkbox set is built from `groups`).

MatchKind.description:
The matched item kind (DEC-12 match ladder: exact display name → alias →
 standard id → fuzzy containment suggestion, in that order; fuzzy is a
 suggestion only).

MatchMode.description: The `required_markers` match mode (the data.py port's `match:` field).

McpSettings.description:
The singleton MCP settings row — the six promoted knobs (agent caps + tool
 caps + pairing-TTL). All fields are `bigint`/`i64` (DEC-5), converted to
 `usize`/`u64`/`Duration` at the read-at-use sites via the accessors below.

action_wall_clock_secs.description:
Outer wall-clock backstop on a single dispatched frontend action, in
 seconds. Source: `agent_channel.rs WALL_CLOCK_CAP` (15 min = 900s).

max_control_sessions.description:
Global cap on live agent control-session connections (OOM guard — SAFETY,
 DEC-3). One session per user, so it effectively caps concurrent AI-paired
 users. Source: `agent_channel.rs MAX_CONTROL_SESSIONS`.

max_inflight_per_user.description:
Per-user cap on concurrent in-flight frontend-action invokes (DoS guard —
 SAFETY, DEC-3). Source: `agent_channel.rs MAX_INFLIGHT_PER_USER`.

max_list_results.description:
Cap on how many capabilities `list_capabilities` returns in one call.
 Source: `handlers.rs MAX_LIST_RESULTS`.

max_result_bytes.description:
Cap on the REST-invoke result body relayed back to the model, in bytes
 (OOM guard — SAFETY, DEC-3). Source: `handlers.rs MAX_RESULT_BYTES` (1 MiB).

pairing_ttl_secs.description:
