 citation the curated rule came from.

match.description: The JSON field is `match` — a Rust keyword, hence the rename.

ResendInvitationResponse.description:
`POST /api/accounts/{account_id}/invitations/{invitation_id}/resend` response.

 **This is the only place a plaintext invitation token is ever surfaced**, and it is
 surfaced to the inviter, who is an `admin` or `owner` of the account the invitation
 belongs to. It is enumeration-safe because the operation is keyed by invitation ID —
 an id the caller obtained by listing their own account's invitations — and takes no
 email, so there is nothing to probe.

invite_token.description:
The freshly minted token. Put it in the FRAGMENT of the invite link
 (`/invite#<token>`) — a fragment is never sent to a server, so it does not reach
 `Referer` headers, proxy access logs or browser history the way a query parameter
 does. Resending invalidates the previous token.

ResolveRequest.description: `POST /api/txr/models/resolve` (PROV-MS-8): the ids to re-verify + hand off.

ResolvedAsset.description:
One verified asset (PROV-MS-8 / CONS-MS-9) — byte-compatible with
 `execution_engine::types::TxrModelAsset`'s `model_ids[]` element so
 `ui-models` passes the response straight through into
 `CreateRunRequest.model_ids` (DEC-10: the join happens at the caller; the
 engine never imports this module).

version.description: The version number to restore (a new head is appended with its bytes).

RootfsStatus.description: Machine-readable rootfs status for the admin UI (`GET /api/sandbox/status`).

content_sha256.description:
The FULL sha256 hex digest of the embedded rootfs (always empty — the
 slot is removed; kept only to preserve the wire shape).

content_version.description:
Short content hash of the embedded rootfs (always empty — the slot is
 removed; kept only to preserve the wire shape).

embedded_bytes.description: Size of the embedded rootfs in bytes (0 — the slot is removed).

extracted.description:
The rootfs has been extracted to the app data dir (always false — see
 the module doc; the digest cache is the live store).

mounted.description:
The rootfs is currently squashfuse-mounted (always false — see the
 module doc; `GET /api/sandbox/envs` reports per-env mount state).

schema_version.description: Embedded schema version the binary expects.

supported.description:
The build embedded a real (non-stub) rootfs (always false — the slot is
 removed).

RunConfig.description:
The run's analysis configuration (board E). Defaults are the documented
 wire defaults (PROV-EE-2); `cpus: null` means "detect at run start"
 (DEC-12) and `label_day: null` means "derive from the file's response_day
 column" (DEC-9's D3 guard).

SandboxAvailability.description: Why the sandbox is (or isn't) available, in machine-readable form.

oneOf.description: Fully initialized — the sandbox is registered and usable.
The host boot probe failed — on Linux this means `bwrap` is not on PATH.

No analysis rootfs was built into this binary (docker absent at build
 time, or a non-Linux build).
The per-job workspace root could not be created.
`init()` has not run yet, or bailed before recording a reason.

SandboxResourceLimits.description:
The singleton resource-limits row. `cpu_max` is bwrap/cgroup's
 `"<quota> <period>"` form (e.g. `"200000 100000"` = 2 cores).

default_env_id.title: 54: the deployment-wide default env-id the sandbox resolves its rootfs for
default_env_id.description:
when neither the per-job converter nor `TXR_SANDBOX_ENV_ID` names one. `None`
 (or empty) = auto-detect from the installed processors' declared `env`, exactly
 as before this row existed. DATA (a manifest-declared env name), not the
 registry security boundary — the registry base stays a compiled read-only const.

staging_timeout_secs.description:
Wall-clock cap on the PRE-SPAWN staging phase of a job (env-image
 resolve/verify/pull/mount + workspace + input materialization). The
 `timeout_secs` budget above only starts once a live child process exists,
 so without this cap anything that stalls before the spawn (hung registry,
 DNS blackhole, stalled TLS handshake, partial pull) pinned the job at
 `running` forever. Operator-facing because the right value depends on
 registry latency + link bandwidth + image size.

updated_by.title: 54: the acting admin stamped on the last PUT (audit; the `*_by` idiom). `None`
updated_by.description:
on the seeded row until the first update. Serialize-only in the API projection;
 never set from a wire body.

SandboxStatus.description: Combined sandbox status for the admin UI.

env_moving_tag.title: 54: the moving `schema<N>-latest-<arch>` tag resolved at pull time — READ-ONLY,
env_moving_tag.description: derived from the binary's rootfs schema + arch.

env_registry_base.title: 54: the env-image registry BASE analyses pull from — READ-ONLY. This is a
env_registry_base.description:
release-time security boundary (a release binary carries no code that could
 redirect a pull elsewhere), so it is DISPLAYED but never operator-writable.

SaveModelsRequest.description:
`POST /api/txr/models/save` (PROV-MS-3): save the run's produced models into
 a new or existing set, optionally keeping the training files + writing the
 one-off `.txr` export.

also_export.description:
Also write `<data_root>/models/exports/<set-name-slug>-<id8>.txr`
 (the "Also save as a file" checkbox).

keep_training_files.description:
Copy the run dir's `input/` files into `<data_root>/models/training/
 <set_id>/` (the L board's "keep the training files" checkbox; default
 false).

method_ids.description: The run's produced models to save (≥ 1 — the run seam's method ids).

source_label.description:
The source file's name the save dialog showed (e.g. `patients.csv`);
 recorded on the set for the I-board "trained on patients.csv" line.
 The engine-grown run `input_summary.file_names.patients` is the
 fallback when omitted (CONS-MS-6b / GAP-D) — always engine truth,
 never the run dir stem.

SaveTarget.description:
The save target — EXACTLY one of the two arms (L's "Name of this set" is
 `set_name`, L2's "into an existing set" is `set_id`). `deny_unknown_fields`
 on the untagged enum makes a payload carrying BOTH arms fail as loud as one
 carrying neither (an untagged match would otherwise silently keep the first
 arm and ignore the second).

SessionSettings.description: Deployment-wide JWT session settings (singleton row). Returned by GET.

refresh_token_expiry_days.description:
Max session length in days (1..=3650) — the refresh-token TTL.
 Active sessions roll on every refresh, so this is the idle bound.

SetDeleteQuery.description:
`DELETE /api/txr/model-sets/{id}` (PROV-MS-4): `keep_files=true` leaves the
 tree + training files and removes the rows only (the I board's "Delete the
 run's models" escape); the default (`false`) is the cascade that prunes
 unreferenced trees.

SetFeatureFlagRequest.description:
`PUT /api/admin/features/{flag_key}` body. `account_id = None` sets the GLOBAL
 default; `Some(_)` sets a per-account override.

SetRoleRequest.description:
`PATCH /api/admin/accounts/{account_id}/members/{user_id}` request — change a
 member's coarse role (#35). Demoting the sole remaining owner is refused (422).

SetSummary.description: A set row of the J/I screens (PROV-MS-4).

source_label.description:
The `patients.csv`-style label the save dialog showed (engine truth,
 never the run dir stem).

StackStatus.description:
The stacked-mode availability half of [`EnvIndexStatus`] (PROV-SS-5).

 `supported` is the host-capability bit the stacked mode shares with the
 shipped sandbox (`SandboxAvailability::Ready` — bwrap + squashfuse + userns
 / `/proc` are all probed at boot); the env-FETCH half (oras) is reported
 separately in `tool_bins` + `reason` because a staged-or-cached deployment
 runs without it (ITEM-6's preflight is the operator's checklist, DEC-16).

reason.description:
The degradation note when something short of hard-unavailable is wrong
 (e.g. `oras` not found for env downloads); `None` when nothing is noted.

registry_base.description:
The compiled txr base-registry prefix — READ-ONLY (a release-time
 security boundary, displayed exactly like
 [`SandboxStatus::env_registry_base`]).

supported.description: The stacked sandbox mode is available on this host.

tool_bins.description:
Map of the host tools the txr env fetch path resolves through
 (`method_env::tool_bin`): `{ "oras": "<path>" | null }`. Machine-
 readable so the admin view can render the exact gap; never trusted for
 anything security-relevant.

StandardId.description: A standard identifier of a file marker column (`(system, id)`).

SyncConnectedData.description:
Handshake payload: the server-assigned connection id. The client echoes it
 back via the `X-Sync-Connection-Id` header on mutations so the fan-out can
 skip the originating connection (self-echo suppression).

SyncEntity.description:
The kind of entity that changed. Serialized snake_case to match the
 frontend's `sync:<entity>` event vocabulary. ADD a variant when wiring a new
 domain; each emitting handler picks the `Audience` explicitly at the
 `publish` call site (there is no central audience table — an owner-scoped
 entity broadcast to everyone would be a leak).

oneOf.description: A durable notification for the user (created/read/deleted). Owner-scoped.
The caller's own profile (display fields / active state). Owner-scoped.

An account the user is a member of changed (created/renamed/deleted).
 Owner-scoped. `id` is the account id.

An account-membership row changed (a member added/removed, or a role
 change). Owner-scoped. `id` is the account id (the changed membership's
 account).

Deployment-wide JWT session settings (singleton). Present so the existing
 auth `SessionSettings` store's `sync:session_settings` subscription has a
 valid entity; the turnkey auth module will emit it once sync-wired.
A user account (admin users list).
A user group (admin groups list; includes group permissions).

An auth provider (local / LDAP / OAuth2 row) was created, edited or
 deleted. Delivered to holders of `auth::providers::read` — published by
 `txresbench-auth`'s admin provider routes through `AuthSyncEntity::AuthProvider`.
 See the `auth_provider` ALLOW_LIST entry in `syncChannelParity.test.ts`:
 this app mounts the admin provider ENDPOINTS but has no admin provider
 UI, so the client half does not exist yet.

The user's session/permissions changed (group membership or a group's
 permissions were edited) — the client re-bootstraps `/auth/me`. `id` is
 the affected user id.

SyncEvent.description: The change notification pushed to clients. Notify-and-refetch only.

SyncSseEvent.description:
The SSE wire enum — the OpenAPI 200-response schema carrier for the subscribe
 stream (`SyncSurface::Wire`). It exists so `SyncEntity`/`SyncAction`/
 `SyncEvent`/`SyncConnectedData` enter the generated `types.ts`; the actual
 stream frames are built by [`sync_event`] / [`connected_event`] below
 (named `event:` + JSON `data:`), matching the SDK `SyncClient`'s wire contract.

TableFormat.description:
The byte format the browser decoded (the server never interprets bytes —
 DEC-1: parsing stays in the browser, rules stay in Rust).

TextRectsQuery.description:
Query for the citation text-rects endpoint: a byte range into the page's
 cleaned text (a chunk's char_start/char_end).

page_w.description:
Rects are fraction-normalized to the page (0..1), origin top-left, so the
 UI overlays them on the page image without knowing the render scale.

Timing.description:
A method's per-fold time estimate fact (median of the benchmark's `status==ok`
 per-fold seconds, or the language fallback with `quality: estimate`).

TimingQuality.description:
Timing fact quality: `measured` from the benchmark's stored per-fold seconds,
 `estimate` from the language-based fallback default.

TxrAppConfig.description:
The sticky E-screen settings (`txr_app_config` singleton; `config: null` is
 an honest never-configured value when the copies were cleared).

TxrAtATimeRequest.description:
The mid-run lane change body (the F board's lane select; GROWN at
 reconcile, CONS-UI-RUN-11).

TxrCoverage.description:
The per-patient coverage record (the board's "needs 3 or more draws; 120 of
 151 have them" is renderable from this).

TxrDeleteQuery.description:
`DELETE /api/txr/runs/{id}` (+ `DELETE /api/txr/runs`): delete_files=false
 keeps the run dir under the app data root (K's "Do not keep copies" sends
 true — DEC-16's mechanics are this flag; history-store owns the policy).

TxrEndpoint.description: The run's endpoint verb (board E's outcome choice).

TxrHistoryBucket.description:
The four-bucket run vocabulary of the K list (DEC-4's map — the engine's
 `creating|preparing|running|finishing` all land in `running`; the K
 display words Done/Failed/Stopped/Running are the consumer's, this node
 delivers the bucket, never display text). The engine-status → bucket map
 lives in the repository (ITEM-2, TEST-HS-4).

cleared_at.description: The last copy-clear stamp (null until one ran — PROV-HS-5).

TxrHistoryDetail.description:
The expanded K block (PROV-HS-3): the row's fields (the summary half,
 spelled out — the detail is a standalone wire shape, not a `flatten` of
 the row: the row's compact `methods` and the detail's rich `methods`
 share one JSON name, and the detail's `models_saved` list replaces the
 row's save flag with the actual records) plus the per-method rows (the
 engine's own [`TxrRunMethod`] verbatim — one vocabulary for F and K),
 the made/used model records, the copies note, the dir size and the
 estimate. `404 RUN_NOT_FOUND` on an unknown id.

dir_bytes.description: The run dir's recursive size when it exists (null when gone).

file_sizes.description:
The input copies' recorded sizes (empty when the copies were cleared
 or the dir is gone).

methods.description:
The run's per-method rows, THE ENGINE'S TYPE verbatim (PROV-EE-3's
 `TxrRunMethod` — the K expanded block's "Methods … 1.0 (2 min)" line
 renders the same row the F screen renders).

models_saved.description: The run's saved models (PROV-MS-11; `[]` when none were saved).

TxrHistoryEstimate.description:
The detail's "took X (estimated Y)" facts (CONS-HS-12): the same
 in-process estimator call the engine's detail uses, projected to the two
 facts the K expanded block renders; `estimate_quality` is the
 catalogue's own vocabulary.

TxrHistoryFileSize.description: One input file copy's recorded size (the detail's "Your files" block).

TxrHistoryItem.description:
One K list row, consumer-shaped (PROV-HS-2): the row's subtitle fields
 (`method_count`, `file_names`, `learned_from`, `predicted`, `endpoint`,
 `decision_day`, `look_ahead_day`), the compact per-method times, the
 first terminal reason (verbatim — K's "Stopped: marker LDH is missing…"
 is the engine's `detail`), the made/used model names (through the
 PROV-MS-11 seam, DEC-9), the retention + capability flags. The meta
 fields come from the engine's own run record — the view is a projection,
 never a parallel model (INV-6).

bucket.description: The DEC-4 bucket the K list filters/renders on.

can_rerun.description:
`copies_kept && bucket != running` — "Run again with the same
 settings" works only while the stored input copies exist (DEC-6).

copies_kept.description:
The retention flag (the retention row's `copies_kept`; a run without
 a row reads `true` — INV-2's conservative default).

counts.description:
The engine's own per-state method counts (the run's `txr_runs.counts`
 JSON verbatim — qa-fixes4 ITEM-2: the K row's status is truthful
 ("Done" only when every method finished; the partial word names the
 failed count), and the counts are the ENGINE's single accounting, the
 same fact the F/G headers render).

elapsed_secs.description: The run's recorded "took" seconds (the K "Took 3 minutes 10 seconds").

estimate_total_seconds.description:
The create-time estimate's total (the K "(estimated 4 minutes)");
 null when never computed (never a fabricated zero).

file_names.description:
The uploaded source names (engine-grown `input_summary.file_names`,
 GAP-HS-1) in the run's own order — never a name derived from the dir
 stem.

id.description: The engine's run id (one entity, one id — DEC-20).

markers_saved.description:
The run produced models that were saved (`run.models[]` non-empty):
 the K row's save semantics — the field is DATA, the rendering is the
 consumer's.

methods.description:
Compact per-method facts only (no per-method body — the row is the
 bounded view, INV-3; the expanded block's rich rows are the detail's
 `methods`).

models_used.description:
The reuse run's consumed set/model names (GROWN at reconcile for
 GAP-HIST-2 — through the engine's `model_ids` over the PROV-MS-11
 seam); `[]` in train mode, never a fabricated name.

predicted.description:
`input_summary.predict_patients` (the "predicted N" figure —
 the predict side's distinct patient count, qa-fixes2 R2-04).

reason.description:
The first terminal method's reason (earliest failed → cannot_run →
 stopped, ITEM-2) — code + detail VERBATIM (CONS-HS-15).

TxrHistoryKind.description:
The K filter's `kind` vocabulary (PROV-HS-2): `learned` = the run's
 `mode: train`, `saved-model` = `mode: reuse` — the engine's own mode
 enum mapped to the filter words, never a third vocabulary.

TxrHistoryListQuery.description:
`GET /api/txr/history` query (PROV-HS-2): `q` = ASCII-folded substring
 over file names / method ids / saved set names (DEC-3 —
 `instr(lower(...), lower($1)) > 0`, no FTS); `kind` = the filter above;
 `status` = ONE bucket or the comma-separated multi-value (GROWN at
 reconcile for GAP-HIST-3: "Stopped or failed" is one call, OR semantics
 — the string is validated/parsed by the repository, ITEM-2); `limit`
 default + clamp per [`HistoryLimits`].

TxrHistoryMethodRef.description:
One compact method ref of the list row (id + version + the recorded
 seconds — the K row's "1.0 (2 min)" facts without a per-method body).

TxrHistoryModelRef.description:
One consumed model reference of a reuse run (GROWN at reconcile for
 GAP-HIST-2: the engine's `model_ids` joined over `txr_model_sets` /
 `txr_models` — the K row's "Model CRC cohort, day 56 on march_new.csv"
 facts; `[]` in train mode).

TxrHistoryModelSaved.description:
One saved model of the run's "Made" record in the detail
 (`txr_models`/`txr_model_sets` joined over `source_run_id` — PROV-MS-11).

TxrHistoryModelsMade.description:
The K "Made: N models (…)" block (PROV-HS-2): `produced` = the run's
 produced-model count, `saved_sets` = the model-store sets whose
 `source_run_id` is this run (PROV-MS-11, DEC-9 — read-only; this node
 never writes a model row).

TxrHistoryPage.description:
One paged history page (PROV-HS-2): newest-first (`created_at DESC`, id
 tie-break), server-side bounded, `total` the engine-truth count under the
 active q/kind/status filters.

TxrHistoryPreferences.description:
The K footer's keep-copies preference (PROV-HS-4): the singleton row
 `txr_history_preferences(id = 1)`, seeded by the migration with the
 board's default `true` — "Copies are kept with this run so it can be
 repeated". The ui-run node reads this route at create time (DEC-13).

TxrHistoryPreferencesUpdate.description:
`PUT /api/txr/history/preferences` body (a missing/typed-wrong field is
 the framework's 422 — serde-validated).

TxrHistorySavedSet.description: One saved set in the "Made" block.

TxrHistoryUsage.description:
The K footer's usage figure (PROV-HS-6): `run_count` from the DB (not
 the walk), the recursive size walk of `rootfs::data_root()` grouped by
 top-level segment (`analysis-*` → runs, `models/` → models, rest →
 other), the user-visible `data_dir` (GROWN at reconcile for GAP-HIST-1 —
 the UI never hardcodes a path and never derives one from a run dir), and
 the stamp.

TxrJoin.description: One confirmed join of a measurements column to the patients table.

key.description: The join key (the column key the validator resolved).

variants.description: The marker variants the column matched (spellings / ids).

TxrLastInputSummary.description: The last input's count facts (what E restores without re-parsing files).

TxrLogStream.description:
A log line's stream (engine-authored state lines vs the method's captured
 stdout/stderr).

TxrMapping.description: One confirmed marker mapping (column key → catalogue marker id).

TxrMethodEnv.description:
The env digest pair recorded on a method row / produced model (base + the
 method's layer — provenance against the manifest, CONS-EE-8).

TxrMethodState.description:
The per-method state machine (INV-2 — one sandboxed environment per method,
 a method never runs twice in the same stack). `cannot_run` is the
 classification verdict from run start (eligibility reason kept on the row);
 `skipped` is a user skip of a waiting/downloading method; `failed` carries
 its `reason`.

TxrModelAsset.description:
A resolved model asset (DEC-10: data, not an import). The engine verifies
 `host_dir` with `tree_sha256` (CONS-EE-6) and binds it read-only; the
 digested env record is provenance against the manifest (EXAMPLE-EE-7).

tree_sha256.description: 64-hex sha256 of the model tree — the verify-before-bind digest.

TxrPhase.description:
The method's execution phase (the F screen's phase column): `env` =
 environment ensure (base + layer), `fit`/`predict` = the two contract
 steps of one `run_method_in_stack` call (X1), `done` = terminal.

TxrPredictionMethod.description:
One finished method's column (prob_source + coverage beside every value —
 INV-3).

label.description:
The column's display name (qa-fixes RES-05): the same `label` the run
 detail's method rows carry — for a reuse run that is the SAVED MODEL's
 name, never the model id's UUID.

TxrPredictionsResponse.description:
`GET /api/txr/runs/{id}/predictions` — one aligned array per patient, one
 entry per finished method (partial while the run continues — the G screen's
 "11 of 12 methods finished" live). A null probability is an abstain; its
 note is carried in the aligned `notes` array.

average.description: Per-patient mean over non-null method values (DEC-11).

patients.description: The predict patient ids, in `test/patients.csv` order.

TxrProbSource.description:
Where a method column's probabilities come from (INV-3: never mixed
 silently in one column; U2 recalibration is recorded per method).

TxrProducedModel.description:
A produced model (X1's `/model` tree + the digests `model-store` binds to —
 PROV-EE-9). `size_bytes` and `own_auc` are known at finalize (the grown
 record, reconcile GAP-B/GAP-C).

tree_sha256.description: Same value as `model_out_digest` — the model-store bind key.

TxrRunCounts.description:
Per-run method-state counts (the F header's done/running/downloading/…
 line, the G header's "11 of 12 methods finished").

TxrRunDetail.description:
The run detail = the summary + the per-method rows + the produced models +
 the derivation facts (PROV-EE-3; the admission + estimate + outcome lines
 of the F/G headers). The summary is FLATTENED so the wire is one object
 (the `sse`/`jobs` precedent of a flat detail payload).

cpus.description: Detected at run start (DEC-12) — the F header's "on <n> CPUs".

estimate.description:
The create-time estimate facts (PROV-MC-6's shape); `None` = never
 computed (a provider failure / an empty queued set — a display fact
 the consumer renders only when the run carries it, D36; never a
 fabricated zero).

memory_total_bytes.description: Read once at run start (Linux /proc/meminfo), display-only (DEC-12).

model_ids.description: The RESOLVED asset ids the reuse run consumed ([] in train mode).

TxrRunEstimate.description:
The run's estimate facts (PROV-MC-6's response shape, stored on the run at
 create — the F header's "about 7 minutes left" source).

schedule_seconds.description:
The lane-packed makespan at the run's at_a_time (estimate-quality per
 method carried by the same provider response).

TxrRunEvent.description:
Frames pushed on `GET /api/txr/runs/{id}/stream`: a run `status`
 change, a per-method `method` transition, a captured `log` line, a
 `progress` sample, or a finished `prediction` column. camelCase event
 names (PROV-EE-4's vocabulary).

TxrRunFileNames.description:
The uploaded source names, captured at create from the parsed tables
 (reconcile GAP-HS-1: never derived from the run dir stem).

TxrRunInput.description:
The input snapshot the engine validates + bundles (CONS-EE-11: it replays
 the SAME parsed tables the screens POSTed — one code path, DEC-15).

joins.description:
The confirmed joins (one per measurement column group; the validator's
 join semantics — CONS-EE-11). Column ids or index keys. Empty = the
 simple one-table case.

keep_copies.description:
K board's "Copies are kept with this run so it can be repeated" —
 default true (DEC-16); the history UI's "Do not keep copies" sends
 false.

mapping.description: The confirmed marker mapping (column key → catalogue marker id).

measurements.description:
The uploaded measurements table (train and predict in one file, or the
 train table when a separate predict file is given).

patients.description:
Training patients (nullable in reuse mode, where the predict table is
 the run's only input).

predict_measurements.description: The separate predict-patients file (path 3: reuse on NEW patients).

TxrRunInputSummary.description:
The input snapshot summary (K's files/settings facts; `markers` = distinct
 resolved marker facts count after joins/mapping).

predict_patients.description:
The predict side's DISTINCT patient count (qa-fixes2 R2-04 — the
 validator's measurements summary; never the row count).

TxrRunListQuery.description:
`GET /api/txr/runs` query (paged — DEC-21; `limit` has the named default +
 ceiling).

TxrRunLogLine.description: One run-scoped log line (the F screen's log panel + "Copy the log").

TxrRunMethod.description: One method's row of the run (the F screen's per-method line).

label.description: The catalogue id (the board's monospace method name).

progress_pct.description:
Download progress only (the manifest size_bytes ratio; null outside
 the env phase).

reason.description:
The failure / cannot-run reason when the row did not reach `finished` —
 INV-2's "failure kept with its reason".

task.description: The outcome task this method ran as (null until classified).

TxrRunMethodFrame.description:
A method-row transition frame (state / reason / phase + the env download
 counters).

TxrRunMode.description:
The run's mode: `train` fits on the uploaded training inputs; `reuse`
 applies resolved saved models (path 3 of the FLOW) — the request then
 carries `model_ids` instead of a training method list.

TxrRunOutcome.description:
The outcome facts of the run (the detail's `task_is_mixed` = the heatmap
 mixes tasks — INV-3's record beside every probability).

TxrRunPredictionFrame.description: A finished-column announcement (the G screen appends the column live).

TxrRunProgressFrame.description:
A progress frame (download pct + fit/predict phase; message is the phase
 line).

TxrRunSettingsView.description:
The expanded-block settings line (from the run's `config` JSON + the
 `txr_runs` columns — PROV-HS-3; `cpus: null` = "detect at run start",
 `seed` is the run's recorded contract seed).

TxrRunStatusFrame.description: A status-transition frame (also the stream's terminal signal).

TxrRunSummary.description: The run row the History list (K) and the F screen header render.

model_ids.description: The RESOLVED asset ids the reuse run consumed ([] in train mode).

TxrTask.description:
The outcome task a method ran as (the enumerated vocabulary ui-results
 normalizes — CONS-UR-8; a run can mix tasks, `task_is_mixed` says so).

UnitFamily.description:
The unit family a marker's values are measured in — the unit-compatibility
 vocabulary of the eligibility engine (a file column in one family never
 satisfies a method needing another).

UnitStatus.description:
The unit verdict of one marker column (DEC-10: `matches` against the
 vocabulary's `canonical_unit`, `family` when only the family agrees, an
 honest `unknown` when nothing is known, `absent` when the file carries no
 unit, `mixed` when the column is not constant).

config.description:
Patch the provider's JSONB config. Empty `client_secret`
 field is treated as "leave the existing value unchanged" so
 admins can edit other fields without re-entering secrets.

UpdateMcpSettings.description: PUT body — every field optional (absent = leave unchanged).

UpdateProfileRequest.description:
Self-service profile update for the authenticated user. Only the
 safe fields are accepted here: `email` is intentionally NOT
 editable (re-verification flow not built; was removed to close an
 OAuth account-takeover vector) and `is_active`/`is_admin`/
 `permissions` are admin-only and can never be set through this path.

UpdateSandboxResourceLimits.description:
A `SandboxResourceLimits` snapshot carrying a job's resolved per-job caps —
 used to drive `CgroupScope::create` on the streaming path (it takes the same
 limits shape the batch path uses). Overlays the resolved profile onto the
 PUT body — every field optional (absent = leave unchanged).

default_env_id.title: 54: deployment default env-id. Absent = unchanged; explicit `""` clears it
default_env_id.description: back to auto-detect (distinct from absent, honored in `merge`/`update`).

UpdateSessionSettingsRequest.description: PUT body for the session settings. Every field optional → absent = leave.

password_changed_at.description:
When the user last rotated their password. NULL means the
 account is still using the bootstrap-issued password (only
 meaningful for the desktop `admin` user). The Remote Access
 module refuses to enable password authentication unless this
 is non-NULL for the admin.

UsesHistory.description:
How much measurement history a method consumes. The manifest vocabulary is
 `landmark | full` (the plan's `none` never occurs in the registry — DRIFT-1
 ITEM-1); `full` renders as "uses all available history".

ValidationMode.description:
The analysis mode: `files` (the complete two-table file set — the C screen)
 or `predict` (measurements only — the N screen, INV-3: the same endpoints
 serve both).

 Wire spelling: the frozen plan (PROV-FV-3) names this value with the
 one word the framework's rename-completeness scan (`scripts/check-no-*
 -domain-literals.sh`) bans across `src-app/**` — the plan's own invariants
 (INV-7, TEST-FV-15) require the shipped module to carry ZERO such tokens.
 The wire spelling here uses the app's own word for the C screen
 (`Files.dc.html` "your files"; the `/files` route of the flow) — the
 two-mode split, the 400 mapping and every test intent are unchanged
 (DRIFT-1 ITEM-2 #1).

ValidationRequest.description:
The validate request body (PROV-FV-3): both tables (or only measurements in
 predict mode), the accepted joins, the confirmed vocabulary mappings and the
 analysis parameters.

ValidationResponse.description:
The validate response (PROV-FV-3): the FULL problem set (per-file +
 cross-table + units + joins + outcome availability), the resolved marker
 columns, both table summaries and the inventory body — the EXACT body of
 `POST /api/methods/eligibility` (CONS-FV-2: the engine replays it
 in-process, so the type is the provider's own).

VocabularyMarker.description:
One vocabulary marker — the `markers[]` entry of the catalogue and the
 vocabulary surface for the upload screen's marker-join offer.

groups.description: Board-group ids this marker belongs to (curated `marker-groups.tsv`).

id.description: The marker id within `system` (e.g. a LOINC code or an HGNC symbol).

n_methods.description: How many runnable methods reference this marker.
